name: Falling With Style
summary: "Falling With Style" is an introductory rite of passage for young Skyborne in Thendal Village. Offered atop the local watchtower by the mischievous Myriaal Mistwake, it challenges novices to test their innate slow-fall ability by leaping from the platform toward Rorian the Dayseeker below.

sections.title: A Leap from the Tower
sections.body: Perched high above Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Myriaal Mistwake invites young Skyborne to test their heritage through a game of daring. Rather than treating their innate magical gifts as sacred relics kept under strict restraint, Myriaal encourages newcomers to leap into the open air from the watchtower ledge. The purpose is practical as well as playful: mastering the instinctive art of walking upon air before life beyond the grove demands it in perilous situations.

sections.title: A Difference in Temperament
sections.body: The exercise serves as a vivid demonstration of two contrasting Skyborne attitudes. While Myriaal delights in sudden descents and startles onlookers for amusement, Rorian the Dayseeker embodies traditional caution. When novices glide down to land squarely before him, Rorian admonishes the reckless display, warning that thoughtlessly exhausting one's magical gifts can leave a traveler helpless when danger strikes. Even so, he concedes that controlled practice within the safety of the village has its place.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this quest?
faq.answer: The quest teaches novice Skyborne how to handle their innate Walk on Air ability, familiarizing them with controlling slow descents from elevated heights.

faq.q: Who gives the quest and where?
aliases: where to start falling with style
faq.answer: It is given by Myriaal Mistwake, who waits atop the wooden watchtower overlooking Thendal Village on Zephras Isle.

faq.q: Who do you land in front of?
faq.answer: You land near Rorian the Dayseeker, a village elder or guardian who is annoyed by Myriaal's antics but accepts the turn-in.

faq.q: Why is Rorian upset by the jump?
faq.answer: Rorian believes innate magical gifts should be conserved and treated with discipline, rather than wasted on practical jokes that startle people.
It teaches the use of Walk on Air, an innate Skyborne ability that slows a character's descent and prevents falling damage.
The exercise takes place in Thendal Village, located on Zephras Isle, the ancestral starting grounds of the Skyborne.

angles.text: This early trial introduces Skyborne novices to the practical mechanics and cultural debates surrounding their innate wind-walking magic.
